rows.comment: The dash clause and 'unaffected' hedge restate the same point in a roundabout way.
lineComments: Fine, states what writes to the band.
Fine, gives the reason: a live connection is required.
The dash is an AI tell; say what the armed alarm does.
rows.replacement:
'Changing the schedule, testing and cancelling all '
'write to the band, so they need a live '
'connection. An alarm that is already armed keeps '
'running on the band.'

rows.comment: Em dash and 'either way' add contrast nobody asked for.
lineComments: Em dash; split into two sentences.
'either way' sets up a contrast with no earlier claim.
rows.replacement:
'Smart wake on. The band still buzzes at the '
'wake time.'

rows.comment: Em dash and wordy; 'Already passed' says it.
lineComments: Em dash and two verbs for one fact.
rows.replacement: 'Already passed'
'Sent, waiting for the band to confirm'

lineComments: 'Latched' is jargon; say confirmed and stored.
rows.replacement: 'The band confirmed it stored the alarm.'

rows.comment: States what happened and what to expect next.
Em dash and run-on; give the two possible causes and the recovery step directly.
lineComments: Em dash and 'there is no way to ask' is roundabout.
Wordy explanation of the same limit.
Recovery step is useful; keep it.
rows.replacement:
'The time above is the last one this app sent. The band '
'has not confirmed it, or you set it in an earlier '
'session, and the app cannot read the alarm stored on '
'the band. Set it again while connected to be sure.'
'Apps that can buzz'

rows.comment: 'Nothing is missed' answers an unraised worry and the dash adds flourish.
lineComments: 'second can buzz' is vague about what happens.
rows.replacement:
'An app appears here after its first notification while '
'the relay is on. That first notification only adds '
'the app to the list. Later notifications from it '
'can buzz.'

rows.comment: Passive and a trailing 'not the exact rhythm' contrast.
lineComments: Passive; make the band the actor.
States the limit of one buzz per pulse.
rows.replacement:
"If Android's vibration pattern cannot be read, the band "
'uses the fallback rhythm below. It plays one buzz per '
'pulse, up to three.'

rows.comment: States the default and a privacy guarantee about Do Not Disturb; keep.
States the off behavior and the same guarantee.
Says what the notice is and which setting governs it.
lineComments: Says what the notice is and when it appears.

rows.comment: Uses 'strap' where the rest of the screen says 'band'.
rows.replacement: 'WHAT MAKES THE BAND BUZZ'

rows.comment: 'It' is vague; say what is unavailable.
rows.replacement: 'Not available on this phone'

rows.comment: Roundabout; state the platform limit directly.
lineComments: 'gives no app that access' is indirect.
rows.replacement:
'Only Android lets an app read which app posted a '
'notification. iOS does not, so Edge cannot relay '
'notifications on this phone.'

rows.comment: Privacy statement kept intact; the dash and passive 'is never read' are removed and the actor named.
lineComments: Says what triggers a buzz; 'strap' changed to 'band'.
rows.replacement:
'The band buzzes when one of the apps below '
'notifies you. Edge never reads or sends what a '
'notification says. It stores only which app posted, '
'on this phone, to build the list.'

rows.comment: Cute contrast title; state the rule.
rows.replacement: 'One buzz per notification'

rows.comment: Dense sentence with semicolon and nested parenthesis; split into one rule per sentence.
rows.replacement:
'Updating a notification does not buzz again. A new '
'notification does. Ongoing notifications such as '
'media players and downloads never buzz. While the '
'band is disconnected nothing buzzes, unless you '
'turn on the phone alert below.'

rows.comment: 'Let us see' is vague; name the app and the permission.
rows.replacement: 'Android must allow Edge to read notifications'

lineComments: Redundant 'that is all this uses it for'.
rows.replacement:
'Edge uses this permission only to read which app '
'posted a notification. The names stay on this phone '
'and nothing leaves it.'

rows.comment: Extraction cut the literal mid-expression; the visible text is a plain status message.
lineComments: Plain status with the failed list interpolated.

rows.comment: Truncated pluralization expression; plain count message.
'It is the complete copy' repeats what the export screen already says.
rows.replacement: 'Database shared.'

rows.comment: Keeps the no-recovery privacy statement; removes the dash and flourish phrasing.
lineComments: Status plus the key fact; dash removed.
'including us' kept as a privacy statement, simplified.
rows.replacement:
'Encrypted backup shared. Without the passphrase nobody '
'can open it, including this app and us.'

rows.comment: Warning with the cost and limit the reader needs.
lineComments: Warning with cost and limit; direct.

rows.comment: Truncated pluralization expression; plain count message.
Dash, list of manual items padded with 'everything', and a vague 'carries where it came from'.
lineComments: Dash after the count; use a colon.
'everything you typed in' is vague; say manual entries.
Say each day lists its source and algorithm version.
rows.replacement:
'${kCsvExportSets.length} CSV files: daily metrics, '
'workouts, sleep, journal, labs and your manual '
'entries. Each day lists its data source and the '
'algorithm version that scored it.'

rows.comment: Fragments and a dash; the privacy warning is kept but stated plainly.
lineComments: 'Lossless' is jargon; restore fact is useful.
Dash and 'anything that opens SQLite' is unexplained.
rows.replacement:
'One .db file with all your data. It is the only format '
'that restores onto another phone. Any SQLite reader '
'can open it, so anyone who gets the file can read '
'your data.'

rows.comment: Dash and 'because there is no account' flourish; keep the no-recovery warning.
lineComments: Vague 'somewhere like iCloud'; tell the reader what to do.
Explanation of the missing account answers nobody; state the consequence.
rows.replacement:
'The same copy as the database export, encrypted with '
'a passphrase. Store it somewhere like iCloud. If '
'you forget the passphrase, the file cannot be opened '
'and there is no recovery.'
